answer: Think of Surveyor engraved map mark filed with the route ledger as a toll booth: each engraved map is a wax seal pressed beside the surveyors mark, so a farm must survey a hundred real boundaries by hand, so the island of passing is trivial for one agent and ruinous for a thousand clones. Clones stop being profitable the moment each one needs its own proof. The summit is the margin: one proof is cheap, a hundred proofs are a business that loses money. The lantern is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
